ai_technology: DBSCAN unsupervised density-based clustering identifies seasonal spatial concentrations in geolocated ranger encounter records.

evidence.ai_role: DBSCAN unsupervised density-based clustering identifies seasonal spatial concentrations in geolocated ranger encounter records.
evidence.tested: Descriptive seasonal clustering of 474 ranger encounters and spatial overlay of forest, roads and crop boundaries.
evidence.unknown: No patrol-effort correction, individual animal identity or prospective deterrence evaluation; summer cluster totals conflict in the source.

organization: Thailand Institute of Scientific and Technological Research

source_review.scope: Primary manuscript Methods, relevant Results, limitations and first-version publication metadata reviewed.

summary: DBSCAN analysis of 474 ranger-recorded gaur encounters in Thailand’s Khao Phaeng Ma Non-Hunting Area identified seasonal concentrations near the western forest boundary, roads and crop plantations. The study used observations from October 2023 to April 2026 to map local forest-agriculture interfaces and inform patrol planning. These are clusters of recorded encounters rather than animal movement or population estimates. Unmeasured patrol effort and missing logging periods can shape the patterns; conflicting summer-cluster counts in the source prevent a precise summer count from being reported.
title: Spatial clustering locates seasonal gaur encroachment patterns
